title: This Machine Builds the Tunnel It Digs
sources: Herrenknecht 'Double Shield TBM' / 'EPB Shield' product pages / Wikipedia 'Tunnel boring machine' / Darda 'Tunnel Boring Machine - Types, Operation & Uses' / Trenchlesspedia 'How Tunnel Boring Machines Work': a tunnel boring machine (TBM) excavates with a rotating cutterhead at the front; disc cutters roll over the rock face under high thrust and fracture it into chips; a cylindrical steel shield behind the cutterhead supports the ground until the lining is in place

Colorado School of Mines 'Segmental Concrete Lining Design and Installation' seminar / Herrenknecht 'Segment production systems' / Wikipedia 'Tunnel boring machine': precast concrete segments are placed by a segment erector inside the shield tail and bolted into complete rings, ring after ring, to form the permanent tunnel lining

City Rail Link (Auckland) 'Our TBM Explained' / emetro.gr 'Hard Rock Shield TBM' / Wikipedia 'Tunnelling shield': hydraulic thrust cylinders (jacks) push against the last installed ring of segments to drive the shield and cutterhead forward
Wikipedia 'Tunnel boring machine' / Trenchlesspedia: excavated material (muck) is carried out of the tunnel by conveyor belt (soft-ground EPB machines use a screw conveyor first, then a belt)

Wikipedia 'Bertha (tunnel boring machine)' / SDOT Blog 'What's Happening, Bertha!' / KNKX 'Bertha, World's Largest Boring Machine, Ready to Dig' / ENR 'Here Comes Bertha: The World's Largest-Diameter Tunneling Machine' / NPR 'Sand Grinds World's Largest Tunneling Machine To A Halt': Bertha, which dug Seattle's SR 99 tunnel, had a cutterhead 57.5 feet in diameter, about five stories tall

lines.text: If you dig a hole sideways under a city, the ground tries to fall back in.
lines.caps: If you dig a hole | sideways under a city, | the ground tries | to fall back in.

lines.text: Loose dirt and cracked rock can cave in as fast as you dig.
lines.caps: Loose dirt and cracked rock | can cave in | as fast as you dig.

lines.text: So, engineers send in a machine that digs and builds the tunnel at the same time.
lines.caps: So, engineers send in | a machine that digs | and builds the tunnel | at the same time.

lines.text: At the front, a giant round cutterhead slowly spins against the earth.
lines.caps: At the front, | a giant round cutterhead | slowly spins | against the earth.

lines.text: Steel disc cutters roll across the rock and crack it into chips.
lines.caps: Steel disc cutters | roll across the rock | and crack it into chips.

lines.text: But even a perfectly round hole can still collapse.
lines.caps: But even a perfectly | round hole | can still collapse.

lines.text: So, a steel shield right behind the cutterhead holds the ground back.
lines.caps: So, a steel shield | right behind the cutterhead | holds the ground back.

lines.text: Inside it, a robotic arm lifts curved concrete pieces called segments.
lines.caps: Inside it, a robotic arm | lifts curved concrete pieces | called segments.

lines.text: It fits them into a full ring, then the next ring, and the next.
lines.caps: It fits them | into a full ring, | then the next ring, | and the next.

lines.text: But how does a machine this heavy move forward with nothing to push on?
lines.caps: But how does a machine | this heavy move forward | with nothing to push on?

lines.text: Hydraulic jacks push against the ring it just built, and shove the whole machine ahead.
lines.caps: Hydraulic jacks push | against the ring it just built, | and shove the whole | machine ahead.

lines.text: Meanwhile, a conveyor belt carries the dirt out behind it.
lines.caps: Meanwhile, a conveyor belt | carries the dirt | out behind it.

lines.text: One machine under Seattle was fifty-seven feet across, about five stories tall.
lines.caps: One machine under Seattle | was 57 feet across, | about five stories tall.

lines.text: You see, it's always pushing off the very tunnel it's building.
lines.caps: You see, it's always | pushing off the very tunnel | it's building.

lines.text: That's why the inside of a subway tunnel looks like a stack of concrete rings.
lines.caps: That's why the inside | of a subway tunnel | looks like a stack | of concrete rings.
